name: Severed Symbiant Variant Maturation Option
body:
Variant Maturation Options

The following option trades out the benefits of the s-class symbiant’s maturation class feature. They can also be gained as archetypes of the standard symbiant or as major convergences.

Some of the options grant symbiant feats, racial traits, or traits. If you already have something the maturation option grants, you can select another in its place.

A severed symbiant has failed to overtake its host, instead becoming less of a parasitic entity and more of a useful tool at the host’s disposal. These symbiants may be inert clones or broken remnants of their once great empire.

Symbiant Bond

A severed symbiant remains bonded to its host after their mental connection is lost, leaving the host to turn its function to their own ends. Each of the benefits here counts as a racial trait when selecting the innocuous spawn symbiant technique. Their values are listed as (x RP).

Reactionary (Ex, 1 RP): Once per day, when the symbiant rolls for initiative, it can roll twice and take the better result. It must decide to use this ability before rolling its check.
Symbiant Strike (Ex, 3 RP): The symbiant’s host gains Improved Unarmed Strike as a bonus feat, and its unarmed strike damage increases to 1d6.
Superior Response (Ex, 1 RP): When forced to make a saving throw, the symbiant can grant its host a +1 bonus to that save as an immediate action.
Unnatural (2 RP): The severed symbiant will sometimes unnerve normal animals, and its host must train to defend themselves against the inevitable attacks from such creatures. The symbiant’s host takes a –4 penalty on all Charisma-based skill checks to affect creatures of the animal type, and receives a +4 dodge bonus to AC against animals. Animals’ starting attitude toward the symbiant is one step worse than normal.
Maturation (Su)

As the host gains greater control over the symbiant, they become able to benefit from its natural attacks and defenses. This does not count as convergence, allowing the host to obtain one in its place.

Powerful Strike: At 5th level, the host’s unarmed strike damage becomes 1d8. At 12th level, it becomes 1d10.
Purity of Body: At 8th level, the host gains immunity to all diseases, including supernatural and magical diseases.
Potent Strike: At 12th level, the host’s unarmed attacks count as cold iron, magic, and silver weapons for the purpose of overcoming Damage Reduction.
Ageless: At 17th level, the host no longer takes penalties to their ability scores for aging and cannot be magically aged. Any such penalties that they have already taken, however, remain in place. Age bonuses still accrue, and the host still dies of old age when their time is up.
Full Control: At 20th level, the host’s unarmed strike damage becomes 2d10 and counts as adamantine for the purpose of overcoming Damage Reduction. The host becomes a magical creature. They are forevermore treated as an outsider rather than a humanoid (or whatever his original creature type was) for the purpose of spells and magical effects. Additionally, the host gains damage reduction 10/chaotic, which allows them to ignore the first 10 points of damage from any attack made by a nonchaotic weapon. Unlike other outsiders, the host can still be brought back from the dead as if they were a member of their previous creature type.

S-Class Characters: Symbiants. Copyright 2025, Samurai Sheepdog. Author: Kevin Glusing
